head_commit.message:
fix: link orphaned landing routes from home and add sitemap lastmod (#962)

Search Console reported /agent-system, /architecture-map, /how-it-works and
/accessibility as "Discovered - currently not indexed" with last-crawled N/A,
and has not queued /tech-radar at all. Nothing was blocking them: all return
200, none carry noindex, robots.txt is Allow: /, and the sitemap reads Success.

The home page footer had drifted from the doc-page SiteFooter — /agent-system,
/architecture-map, /tech-radar and /storybook/ were reachable only from pages
Google has not fetched yet, so they sat one hop behind an uncrawled page. / is
the only URL with real crawl equity. This is the same orphan class #934 fixed
for /how-it-works, so HomeBody.test.tsx now asserts every sitemap route is
linked from home; it fails today if any link is removed.

Sitemap entries also carry a hand-kept lastmod from each route's last
content-bearing commit, rather than a build-time timestamp that would churn on
every deploy.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
feat: add exa as a fallback web-search backend for company research (#961)

* feat: add a pluggable web-search backend with exa as the fallback

Company research runs on the active AI provider's own web search, which leaves a
whole population with nothing: local Ollama without an ollama.com account key,
every `openai-compatible` gateway, and any provider whose search isn't wired up.
They get a silently empty brief, and the cover letter is written with no company
knowledge - indistinguishable from one written with a full brief.

The seam was already there. `research.rs` is provider-agnostic (SearchResult,
the query builders, the synth prompts, the injection guard), and the three
`ollama_research*` functions were each "search -> if empty return '' ->
synthesize with the provider's own model". Only the search step was ever
Ollama-specific.

So this extracts that step behind a `WebSearcher` trait, moves the three
pipelines to `search/` as `searched_research*`, and adds `ExaSearcher`
(api.exa.ai/search, `ai:exa` key). All three research facets - company, salary,
per-question answers - gain the fallback at once.

Selection is FALLBACK-ONLY and decided from configuration before any call: a
provider that can already search keeps using its own, even with an Exa key
stored, so nobody silently starts paying a second vendor. A native search that
runs and returns empty is NOT retried against Exa - one pass, one search, one
vendor sees the query. `resolve_search_backend` is a pure predicate so that
policy is testable, and inverting it fails a test.

Synthesis deliberately stays on the user's own model. Exa's own answer endpoint
would be fewer calls but would bypass both `SYNTH_SYSTEM`'s prompt-injection
guard (search results are attacker-reachable text) and the `is_no_info` filter.

The fallback lands on the trait's DEFAULT `research()`, so providers with native
search override it and are untouched, and a new provider with no search inherits
it for free - no per-provider change either way.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: report whether research can actually run, and add the exa key ui

`supportsWebSearch` reported what a provider ADVERTISES. Local Ollama advertises
web search for the family, so a keyless install showed the "search company"
toggle ON and returned an empty brief every single time - a state the user
cannot act on, because nothing told them a key was missing.

It now answers whether a search backend is CONFIGURED: the provider's own model
searches, or its searcher has a key, or a fallback backend does. Keyless Ollama
reads false, which is the truth.

Three parts:

- `search::research_available` is the single source, used by both the renderer
  probe and the server-side per-question gate. That gate previously read the
  static capability, so it would have skipped (and mis-charged) a keyless
  install that has a working fallback - the trait method is now
  `research_available()`, which is also what the test fakes assert on, so the
  two can't drift.

- `ai_model_capabilities` takes `AppHandle` to read stored keys. The renderer
  signature is unchanged (Tauri injects it), but the key mutations now
  invalidate the capabilities query: it caches with a VERY_LONG staleTime, so
  without that, adding a key left the toggle wrong until restart.

- Settings → Company Research grows a second key slot. The existing field was
  hardcoded to `ollama-cloud`; the two differ only in labels and credential
  slot, so it is parameterised rather than copied. Both go through the existing
  key IPC, which already accepts an arbitrary slot name - no new commands.

The section copy states the fallback-only rule explicitly, so a user adding an
Exa key knows it will not take over from a provider that already searches.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: record the search-backend axis and refresh the stale limit docs

ADR-0023 records why web search is a separate axis from generation, and the three
sub-decisions that each had a real alternative: fallback-only (not Exa-preferred),
no second chance on an empty native search, and synthesis staying on the user's
own model rather than using Exa's answer endpoint - which would bypass both the
prompt-injection guard and the no-info filter.

ADR-0005 needs no amendment and the ADR says so explicitly: Exa is a new vendor
inside the already-enumerated class 3 (web search, opt-in), not a new egress
class, and it receives exactly what the current search already does. Its
consequence - keep the enumeration accurate - is honoured in README and
SECURITY, which now name Exa within that class.

`docs/CONTEXT.md` gains **search backend**, the term this feature creates: it
retrieves, it cannot generate, and it is not an AI provider. Without it, "search
provider" would have drifted into use for something deliberately absent from
`ProviderId` and the provider picker.

Two fixes to `anti-abuse-limits.md` that were already stale, one of them my own:

- The concurrency guard stopped being a counter in #960 and became a semaphore
  permit with two admission styles (reject vs wait), and I did not update the
  doc then.
- The daily ceiling is keyed by VENDOR, not by `ProviderId` - which is what lets
  a search backend charge its own bucket instead of spending the AI provider's.

Also replaced two line-number references with symbol names; they had already
drifted and would drift again.
